summary: Iter76 (Seasons + Sign-Up remind-claimed) tested end-to-end. Backend: 32/32 pytest cases PASSED covering Seasons CRUD, single-active invariant, activate, patch validation, rollover (target/kinds + multi-season membership), season filter includes unassigned, edit_scope='this' fork, edit_scope='all' in-place, delete-active promotes next + detaches season_ids, delete 404, POST /api/team/signups/{id}/remind-claimed (sent/no_phone/failed shape + Twilio magic number send), regression on /remind, and unfiltered list endpoints. Frontend (Expo Web, 390x844): login → dashboard renders SeasonBar; when no seasons, shows 'Create a season' empty chip; after creating TEST_UI_S1 in /seasons, dashboard SeasonBar shows 'All seasons' + season chip + manage gear; row shows Active badge; chip tap filters the dashboard; delete via row menu removes it. Sign-up sheet Edit modal has both testIDs signup-remind and signup-remind-claimed in code and backend verified them working. All test data cleaned up.
critical_code_review_comments: core/helpers.season_query: the '$or' clause uses {'season_ids': {'$in': [None, []]}} to match unassigned items. MongoDB {'$in': [None]} matches missing/null fields (works for legacy docs). It does NOT match documents whose season_ids is an empty array [], BUT the separate {'$exists': False} branch AND the {'$in':[[]]} literal do together give correct coverage in practice (empty array literal in $in matches empty array field). Verified by test: unassigned athlete with season_ids: [] shows under both S1 and S2 filters. No fix needed, but consider simplifying with a clearer expression like {'$or':[{'season_ids': season_id}, {'season_ids': {'$in': [None]}}, {'season_ids': {'$size': 0}}, {'season_ids': {'$exists': False}}]} for readability.

routers/seasons.delete_season: promotes 'first remaining season' by order asc but doesn't consider is_active fallback if none exists — acceptable since delete is idempotent and next call to activate resolves it.
routers/seasons.rollover: uses $addToSet so re-running rollover is idempotent (good). Returns modified_count which could be 0 if already rolled; consider surfacing that to UI.
seed_data_creation: Only ephemeral TEST_* seasons, athletes, signup sheet and roster members — all cleaned up in teardown fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login: /login page uses testIDs login-email-input, login-password-input and a native 'Sign in' button (submit via clicking the button, NOT Enter-key which triggers a 401). SeasonBar hides when no seasons exist; shows empty 'Create a season' chip via testID seasonbar-create. Once ≥1 season exists it shows testIDs seasonbar-all + seasonbar-{season_id} + seasonbar-manage. /team/signups uses testID signup-add for the '+' add-sheet button; the create-modal name input has no distinct testID (falls back to plain <input>). Signup Edit modal exposes signup-remind and signup-remind-claimed side-by-side. Backend remind endpoints require Premium (apple review account is admin so passed after self-toggle in test). Twilio magic number +15005550006 is safe for send tests.
